title: WHAT IF YOU WENT BACK TO 2010 WITH $100?

segments.line: So, what do you buy?
Not toys. Not trainers. You buy the strangest thing in 2010.
Bitcoin.
Right now almost nobody has heard of it. It's a nerdy experiment on a forum.
A coin is worth less than a penny.
On the twenty- second of May, a man in Florida pays ten thousand bitcoins for two pizzas. That's real.
So you find someone on the forum, and you send them your hundred dollars.
They send you ten thousand coins. The same pile that just bought two pizzas.
They think you're an idiot. You let them.
Then you wait. You can't tell anyone. You can't touch it. You
just check the price, every single night, under the covers.
And while you wait, you have a little fun.
Your best friend Mo is obsessed with the World Cup.
You tell him Spain will win the final. One– nil. A goal from Iniesta, in extra time, in the one hundred and sixteenth minute. Mo
laughs at you.
Then on the eleventh of July, the ball hits the net in the one hundred and sixteenth minute.
Mo stares at you like you're a ghost. 'Do it again. ' So you do. You
tell him a photo app called Instagram is coming in October. It comes in October. You tell
him about a block game called Minecraft that everyone will be playing. He thinks it looks terrible.
Now he's building a castle every night.
Then, in February 2011, it happens. One bitcoin is worth one dollar.
Your hundred dollars just became ten thousand.
In early June, it hits thirty- one dollars.
Your hundred dollars is now worth three hundred and ten thousand.
You're a kid, and you're secretly richer than everyone on your street.
Mo whispers, 'How? ' You just say, 'Pizza. '
But here's the thing about magic internet money. It can disappear just as fast.
